title: Payload-split journey UX notes and wireframe iteration
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a focused UX iteration for a token-level cost + latency breakdown view that emphasizes 'payload-splitting' (breaking an invocation into request payload segments, token spans, and downstream compute phases) rather than only per-token lists. The goal is a diagnostic panel that surfaces the dominant contributors to cost and tail latency for a single invocation and for aggregated slices (by prompt type, model, route).

Context / why this differs from previous work:
- Existing artifacts focus heavily on per-token waterfalls and token timelines. This iteration experiments with a hybrid timeline + span-based inspector (think: HTTP waterfall but for tokens/KV/cache/compilation phases).
- We want this view to be immediately actionable for SRE / platform engineers (isolate slow KV cache hits, batching stalls, or model variant fallbacks) and product engineers (which prompt fragments are driving cost).

Primary user stories:
1) As an SRE I want to scrub a single slow invocation to see whether network, KV cache miss, or attention computation caused the tail so I can triage spin-up vs model bug.
2) As a Product PM I want to compare the same prompt across 50 invocations to find which prompt fragments cause higher token churn/cost.
3) As an ML engineer I want to see when quantized kernels increased latency vs float kernels under long contexts.

High-level interactions (MVP):
- Invocation timeline at the top: compact bar for phases (parse, prefix-lookup, kv-cache-access, batch-queue, model-exec, post-process). Click a phase to expand per-token timing in the lower pane.
- Payload-split lanes: split the invocation by logical 'payload segments' (system prompt, user prompt, tool output, user follow-ups) so we can attribute cost/latency to the semantic piece, not only token index.
- Token-slice inspector (bottom-left): when a phase is expanded, show a horizontal token strip with color overlays for exec-time/cost intensity and hover-to-see token text + token-cost estimate.
- Pathway inspector (bottom-right): show dependency graph between phases and any external calls (DB lookup, tool call, model fallback). This is a small force-directed mini-graph showing which external hop added latency.
- Aggregate compare mode: inline toggle to switch to 'slice-aggregate' where the same UI shows distributions across N invocations (p95, median, count) with heatmap brush to pick outliers.

Wireframe notes (sketch to implement):
1) Header strip - Invocation summary: id, model, variant, region, total tokens, total cost (USD est), total latency, timestamp. Small pill icons for "KV cache hit rate" and "fallbacks".
2) Timeline bar (single row) - timeline is scaled to total invocation latency. Each phase is a segment; widths proportional to time. Phases are clickable and keyboard-accessible.
3) Payload lanes - vertical lanes beneath timeline: each lane is labeled (system / user / tool / assistant). Each lane shows token spans as boxes, stacked horizontally aligned to the timeline. Boxes carry color saturation for cost density.
4) Token inspector - shows 160px-high horizontal strip; tokens rendered as small chips (lean UI). Chips show hover card: token text, token index, token-cost estimate, time spent in selected phase. Chips are selectable to pin for side-by-side compare.
5) Pathway inspector - minimal network graph; nodes are labeled (kv-cache, model-variant-a, scheduler, external-api). Edge thickness encodes average latency across selected invocations. Clicking a node filters timeline to hops involving that node.
6) Suggested fixes rail (right column) - automated heuristics produce 0–3 suggestions: e.g., "Consider enabling prefix-KV caching for route X; estimated 18% cost reduction", "Try variant-quant-async for high throughput use-cases". Each suggestion is accompanied by a confidence badge and a button to create a ticket.

Data considerations / instrumentation required:
- Align RPC spans from serving runtime with token indices. Need a lightweight map: span_id -> [token_start, token_end], span_type, start_ts, end_ts, resource_id.
- Cost attribution heuristics: token-cost = token compute time * model-cost-per-GPU-ms / effective-occupancy. This is approximate; must be labeled as estimate.
- Privacy: when showing token text in shared views, redact PII by default (config flag in console).

Grooming backlog (rough priorities):
- CONS-4321 (P0): wireframe -> prototype HTML/CSS timeline + token-strip (owner: Samir) - acceptance: click-expand phase, hover token shows meta.
- CONS-4332 (P1): backend span-token alignment endpoint (+ sample exporter) - acceptance: example trace with token spans from prod sampling.
- CONS-4333 (P1): suggestion heuristics mock service (rule-based) - acceptance: 3 canned rules show up in rail.
- CONS-4340 (P2): aggregate compare heatmap + brush - acceptance: user can select a percentile range and see filtered timelines.
- CONS-4354 (P2): pathway inspector graph backend metrics (node latency aggregation) - acceptance: edges populate with p50/p95 labels.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Single-invocation timeline loads within 300ms for sampled traces (frontend renders quickly with placeholders).
- Phase expansion shows per-token timing for at least first 512 tokens.
- Suggestion rail returns deterministic 0–3 items for visible invocation.

Edge cases & UX guards:
- Very long contexts (>4096 tokens): show sampled tokens with a slider to adjust sampling density; default to contiguous first/last token sampling.
- Missing spans: fall back to per-phase aggregates and surface "span instrumentation missing" callout with link to docs.
- Cost accuracy caveat: badge in header "estimated" with tooltip explaining formula.

Data examples (for prototype):
- Invocation A (short): total latency 420ms, phases: parse 8ms, kv-cache 22ms (miss), batch-queue 14ms, model-exec 360ms, post 16ms. Payload lanes: system (0.5 tokens), user (34 tokens). Token inspector shows token 12 had exec spike (45ms) due to fallback.
- Aggregation example: 100 invocations of route /chat: p50 latency 180ms, p95 610ms; heatmap shows tail correlated with "external-tool" node latency.

Open questions to resolve:
- What sampling rate from production traces is acceptable for the console? (SRE input required)
- How to represent preemptible / burst compute billing differences in the cost estimator? (Finance and billing required)
- Should suggestions be writable to infra-as-code templates (i.e., autopatch route config)? Risky — need security review.

Next steps / owners:
- Prototype HTML/CSS timeline & token-strip (Samir) - due: 2026-03-10
- Backend span-token alignment API spec (Ava) - due: 2026-03-03
- Heuristics list + examples (Elena) - due: 2026-02-28
- Sync with SRE and Billing for sampling and estimator inputs (Rory) - meeting: 2026-02-20 notes in CONS-4321.

Meeting notes snapshot:
- 2026-02-12 workshop: agreement to prefer span-first timeline to long token lists for initial release; suggestion rail should include confidence and rough savings. SRE asked for per-host sampling flags.

Quick sketch checklist (for implementation handoff):
- [ ] HTML timeline component (accessible, keyboard nav)
- [ ] Token strip component with hover cards and pin state
- [ ] Right rail suggestions component w/ call-to-action to create ticket
- [ ] Backend: span-token alignment endpoint + example exporter
- [ ] Docs: instrumentation guide + privacy redaction toggle

Rough UI copy (for designers):
- Header total cost label: "Estimated token cost: $0.0087 (approx)"
- Phase tooltip: "Model exec — 360ms — 86% of invocation time"
- Suggestion tile title: "Enable route-level prefix cache" + small subtitle "Est. 18% cost reduction for chat completions"

Notes to self:
- Keep the prototype intentionally lightweight; we should not attempt to render multi-thousand token lists in the MVP. Sampler + good defaults will make this feature usable quickly.

Attachments / artifacts to include in prototype folder:
- sample-trace-2026-01-23.json (mock)
- low-fi-timeline-sketch.png (designer)

-- end of note --
